pages.title: A closed population with three states
pages.text:
A closed population with three states
S + I + R = N.
Susceptible, infectious, and recovered are mutually exclusive categories.
Recovery retains people inside the population; it removes infectiousness, not population
mass.

pages.title: Recovery as a transition hazard
pages.text:
Recovery as a transition hazard
Jrec = γI.
A constant hazard gives survival in the infectious state proportional to e−γt.
It does not give everyone the same recovery date.

pages.title: The invariant population simplex
pages.text:
The invariant population simplex
S, I, R ≥ 0, S + I + R = N.
At an empty donor group, its outﬂow vanishes.
S cannot increase and R cannot decrease.
Mathematical Modeling Notes 7 / 20

pages.title: The peak is a balance of flows
pages.text:
The peak is a balance of ﬂows
Sp = N γ/β.
As S falls, infection recruitment eventually falls below recovery.
The peak can occur with many susceptible people remaining.

pages.title: An analytic orbit relation
pages.text:
An analytic orbit relation
I − I0 = −(S − S0) + γNβ log SS0 .
The logarithm acts on a dimensionless ratio.
This relation checks the trajectory independently of its time parametrization.
Mathematical Modeling Notes 13 / 20

pages.title: One conservative numerical step
pages.text:
One conservative numerical step
S+ = S − hJinf ,
I + = I + h(Jinf − Jrec),
R+ = R + hJrec.
Compute each ﬂux once and use it in both aﬀected equations.
Mathematical Modeling Notes 15 / 20

The one-day hand calculation

pages.title: A sufficient positivity restriction
pages.text:
A suﬃcient positivity restriction
S+ = S(1 − hβI/N ), I + = I(1 − hγ) + hβSI/N.
h max(β, γ) ≤ 1
ensures nonnegative states throughout the simplex.
Mathematical Modeling Notes 17 / 20

Changing one transmission parameter
For β = 0.08, γ = 0.1 day −1:
βS0/N − γ = −0.0208 day −1.
Since S cannot increase, infectious prevalence declines from the start.

pages.title: Verification of trajectories and observables
pages.text:
Veriﬁcation of trajectories and observables
Check S + I + R, nonnegativity, monotonic S, R, and the analytic orbit.
Reﬁne h at common times; compare peak height and time separately.
Conserved population does not imply an accurate epidemic curve.
Mathematical Modeling Notes 19 / 20

pages.text:
Evidence for a population model
Document contact assumptions, observation process, initial conditions, and parameter
units.
A continuous hazard and a discrete infection probability are diﬀerent quantities.
Synthetic scenario comparison is not empirical validation.
